Based on my search, here are the typical jersey numbers for linebackers in football:

## NFL Linebacker Jersey Numbers

**Current NFL Rules (2023 and beyond):**
- **Primary range:** 0–59 and 90–99

This represents a significant expansion from earlier years. The NFL has updated its numbering rules multiple times to give players more flexibility:

| Era | Linebacker Number Range |
|-----|------------------------|
| Pre-1973 | No standardized system |
| 1973–1984 | 50–59 only |
| 1984–2015 | 50–59 and 90–99 |
| 2015–2021 | 40–59 and 90–99 |
| 2021–2023 | 0–59 and 90–99 |

## Most Traditional/Classic Linebacker Numbers

While linebackers can now wear numbers from 0–59 and 90–99, the **most traditional and commonly associated numbers** are:

- **50–59** — The original linebacker numbers since 1973
- **90–99** — Added in 1984, very popular for linebackers

Some iconic linebacker numbers include:
- **40–49** — Became available in 2015; notable examples include Devin White (#40 at LSU)
- **50–59** — Classic middle linebacker range (e.g., Dick Butkus #51, Mike Singletary #50)
- **90–99** — Popular for outside linebackers and pass rushers

## College Football

College football is much less restrictive — linebackers can wear **any number from 0–99**, with the only major rule being that at least five offensive linemen must wear 50–79.

## Key Takeaway

If you're looking for the **most typical or "classic" linebacker numbers**, **50–59** remain the most iconic and traditionally associated with the position, though **90–99** is also extremely common. With recent rule changes, single-digit numbers (0–9) and numbers in the 40s are increasingly seen as well.

Sources:
1. https://operations.nfl.com/the-rules/rules-changes/nfl-jersey-numbers/
2. https://touchdowntrips.com/nfl-jersey-numbers-explained/
3. https://www.jt-sw.com/football/pro/index.nsf/Documents/0-jers-nums
4. https://www.metroleague.org/nfl-jersey-numbers-list_af/
